_readme: The 9-slide webinar storyline Alex describes at 46:59-48:09 in the 2026-09-04 sales training. He was pointing at a list on his screen ('it's like 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9') and narrated each step aloud. These are the STEPS - the job each slide does - not the headlines. Headlines are written per prospect from the brief.
_lineage: Fireflies transcript -> the brief (extracted_data) -> these slides. Every slide declares the brief field it reads from in 'source'. Where source is null the brief has no field for it yet and the copy here is INFERRED - Geri's transcript-to-brief step needs to start emitting those four.
_style: Sparse. Alex: 'probably you give them one sentence to it', 'just one sentence, like really'. The whole storyline is 'two, three minutes' across nine slides - about fifteen seconds each. A headline and one line. Never a paragraph.
_case_study_warning: Slide 6 is the PROSPECT'S case study - one of THEIR clients, shown to THEIR audience. It is NOT a Quantum Scaling client. The QS case-study library (Airtable) is used on the Lead List and Calendar Invite, where we are proving OUR results to the prospect. Different direction. Do not wire Airtable into this slide.

slides.headline: Your margin isn't leaking in the machines. It's leaking in the handoffs.
slides.line: A 90-minute working session for industrial operators carrying cost they can't see.

slides.headline: Built for one room, not a general audience.
slides.line: COOs and VP Operations at 50-500 person industrial and manufacturing firms across North America and Western Europe.

slides.headline: Referrals stopped scaling, and nothing replaced them.
slides.line: Growth is entirely referral-driven and has flattened - with no repeatable way to reach new operators.

slides.headline: Another year of this is a seven-figure decision.
slides.line: Three retainer clients a month, not won, at a $32,000 deal size, is roughly $1.1M of contracted revenue that never enters the pipeline.
slides.inferred_from: extracted_data.goals (3 retainers/mo) x extracted_data.business.deal_size ($32,000). The brief has no 'impact of not changing' field.

slides.headline: Three new retainers a month. No new delivery hires.
slides.line: Operating cost per unit down 18-30% within two quarters.

slides.headline: A 200-person plastics manufacturer in Ohio.
slides.before: Changeover eating a full shift; margin invisible below the line item.
slides.note: The PROSPECT'S client, not ours. Dummy data in the prototype - in production this comes from the prospect's own case study in the brief.

slides.headline: From this call to first result in about a quarter.
slides.line: A 9-week sales cycle, then two quarters to the cost curve bending. You will know inside 90 days whether it is working.
slides.inferred_from: extracted_data.business.sales_cycle (9 weeks) + result_delivered timeframe. The brief has no explicit journey/timeline field.

slides.headline: Four risks, taken off your side of the table.

risks.answer: Paid from the saving, not from budget.
Diagnosis first. If the numbers aren't there, we say so.
One operator on point. Not an account team.
Your team stays on delivery. We do the build.

slides.inferred_from: Alex names these four risks verbatim at 47:54: 'the investment risk, the failure risk, the communication gap risk, the time investment risk'. The ANSWERS are inferred - the brief has no risk-handling field.

slides.step: The offer, and three ways in
slides.headline: Operational turnaround for industrial firms under margin pressure.
slides.line: Three ways to start - each one gives you something whether or not you go further.

ctas.detail: We map where cost is escaping. You keep the map.
See the system running on your numbers, not ours.
90 minutes with an operator who has done it.

slides.inferred_from: Alex at 48:00: 'three key CTAs that are high value with a deep analysis of their situation and create a custom demo'. The brief has no CTA field.
